evidence.title: Harnessing surface chemistry: a comprehensive review on the role of functional groups in antifouling membrane design.
evidence.abstract: Membrane fouling remains a major barrier to reliable and cost-effective water treatment, motivating surface engineering strategies that suppress foulant attachment while preserving permeability and selectivity. This review critically examines antifouling membrane design through a functional-group-centred framework, focusing on grafted monomers and polymer architectures that regulate interfacial hydration, charge, polarity, and steric interactions. Oxygen-, nitrogen-, sulfur-, phosphorus-containing, zwitterionic, and multifunctional chemistries are comparatively evaluated across organic fouling, biofouling, colloidal deposition, and scaling. The analysis demonstrates that antifouling performance is governed not only by functional group identity but also by grafting density, chain conformation and mobility, spatial uniformity, and anchoring stability. Oxygen-rich and zwitterionic interfaces suppress foulant attachment primarily through strong hydration, while nitrogen-containing chemistries offer tuneable charge and antimicrobial functionality. Sulfur- and phosphorus-containing groups provide additional hydration and ion-coordination capabilities. However, no single chemistry is universally optimal across feed conditions. Major barriers to translation include reliance on short-term single foulant testing, limited cyclic cleaning and ageing studies, and inadequate verification of long-term graft stability. Future research should therefore prioritise durable multifunctional interfaces, standardised testing under realistic conditions, scalable grafting routes, and data-driven optimisation of structure-property-performance relationships.

evidence.title: Combining Topography and Chemistry toward Polydopamine Antibacterial Surfaces
evidence.abstract: Microporous antibacterial surfaces offer a promising route for preventing bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation, yet their fabrication often involves complex and energy consuming processes. In this work, we present a sustainable strategy for producing multifunctional antibacterial surfaces by combining a microporous cellulose acetate butyrate (CAB) substrate, a bioinspired polydopamine (PDA) coating, and in situ synthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs). CAB, selected for its film-forming capability and ease of microstructuring via spin-coating, provides a tunable platform for topographical control. PDA, formed through the oxidative self-polymerization of dopamine, serves as a conformal adhesive layer and simultaneously acts as a reductive matrix for AgNP formation. Immersion in silver nitrate solution enables the direct deposition of AgNPs without external reducing agents, facilitated by the catechol functionalities of PDA. The resulting CAB–PDA–AgNP surfaces exhibit enhanced antibacterial activity through the combined effects of patterning, surface chemistry, and silver-mediated bactericidal action. The fabrication process is low-energy and solvent-minimized, aligning with principles of sustainable material development and offering a versatile platform for antibacterial coatings.

evidence.title: An Ion‐Based Strategy Toward Synergistic Surface Functionalization Combining the Osteogenic Properties and NIR‐Mediated Antibacterial Activity of PEEK
evidence.abstract: Persistent implant‐associated infections critically compromise the longevity and success of orthopedic prostheses. Herein, we present a facile surface‐engineering strategy to construct a multifunctional PEEK‐based implant by introducing manganese‐chelated polydopamine (Mn@p) and mesoporous bioactive glass nanoparticles (MBGNs) onto sulfonated PEEK (SPEEK). The resulting Mn@p/MBG‐SPEEK exhibits a hierarchically porous three‐dimensional architecture with markedly enhanced hydrophilicity and surface roughness. This tailored interface shows in vitro bioactivity and cytocompatibility, significantly promoting the osteogenic differentiation of MC3T3‐E1 cells through the activation of PI3K/Akt/mTOR and AP‐1 signaling pathways, as evidenced by the upregulation of ALP, OCN, OPN, and Runx2 expression. Meanwhile, the pro‐angiogenic potential of Mn@p/MBG‐SPEEK is supported by the upregulation of VEGF and CD31 in HUVECs and enhanced capillary‐like network formation. Notably, Mn@p/MBG‐SPEEK demonstrates efficient light‐to‐heat conversion and potent antibacterial efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus under near‐infrared (NIR) irradiation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that Mn chelation narrows the HOMO‐LUMO energy gap and facilitates charge separation, thereby amplifying photothermal and ROS‐mediated antibacterial effects. Collectively, this study establishes a versatile and scalable route to enhance the biological performance of PEEK implants, offering a conceptual framework for integrating ion‐assisted therapy with phototherapy toward next‐generation bioactive and infection‐resistant orthopedic materials.

evidence.title: When a Sensor Loses Its Oracle: Three-Arm Differential Observability and Zero-Oracle Fail-Closed Abstention for Membrane Fouling Diagnostics
evidence.abstract:
Soft sensors for reverse osmosis (RO) and forward osmosis (FO) desalination must separate reversible concentration polarization (CP) from irreversible mineral scaling and biofouling while remaining resilient to sensor drift, temperature shocks, and reference-channel contamination. We identify two structural vulnerabilities in differential membrane diagnostics: (1) a 2-arm differential cartridge cannot distinguish reference-arm contamination from test-arm cleanliness, producing a 71.17% estimation error without warning under 10% partial reference fouling (Scenario NC5), whereas a 3-arm differential manifold with a witness-ratio guard (τref = |rref(t) − rref,0|/rref,0 > 0.03) restores Rank-2 Fisher observability (det I > 0) and cuts error to 7.72%; and (2) autonomous diagnostic codebases suffer from oracle leakage when simulator ground-truth fields (ground_truth_scale_um) or synthetic nominal reference values remain accessible inside production classes or when invariants rely on strip-prone assert statements under python -O. After hardening CommercialPhysicalWitnessB (removing all simulator fields, enforcing explicit runtime ValueError guards across 19/19 standard and -O unit tests), the zero-oracle estimator achieves 5/5 (100%) clean operating-sweep coverage and reduces false-confident commits on 9 adversarial fault challenges from 7/9 (77.8%, SystemA) and 8/9 (88.9%, SystemC/R0) to 1/9 (11.1%, residual C07 80 nm sub-resolution CaSO4 film), while correctly abstaining (21/21 ABSTAIN_MISSING_REFERENCE_EVIDENCE) on 21 published literature rows that lack a physical reference channel.

Evidence classification: simulation only (SIMULATION_VERIFIED_WET_LAB_UNTESTED). No wet-lab membrane experiment has been executed; zero wet-lab membrane hours. Published as a methods protocol / registered-protocol preprint, not as experimental results. The \$551.32 COTS benchtop flow-loop protocol in Section 3 is pre-registered and specified, not run. All metrics are simulation replays and literature-row audits, deterministically reproduced by reproduce_paper2_zero_oracle_pareto.py, included in the reproducibility bundle. Reproducibility code in the bundle is Apache License 2.0; paper text is CC BY 4.0.

evidence.title: Plasma-Enhanced Magnetron Sputtering: A Novel Approach for Biofunctional Metal Nanoparticle Coatings on Reverse Osmosis Composite Membranes
evidence.abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is the most common method for treating salt and brackish water. As a membrane-driven process, a key challenge for RO systems is their susceptibility to scaling and biofouling. To address these issues, functional coatings utilizing metal nanoparticles (MNPs) are developed. In this study, silver, gold, and copper nanoparticles are applied onto thin-film composite (TFC) membranes using plasma-enhanced magnetron sputtering. The elemental composition, surface morphology, and hydrophilicity of the coatings are analyzed using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and contact angle measurements. The antimicrobial properties and the filtration efficiency of the coated membranes are assessed through application-specific experimental setups. Silver and copper nanoparticles exhibit superior antimicrobial properties, reducing microorganism adhesion by a factor of 103 compared to uncoated membranes. Under appropriate coating conditions, no deterioration in filtration performance is observed. Enhancing the adhesion of MNPs is necessary for achieving sustained release of metal ions.

The ten English research-design manuscripts contain 7,770 pages, 300 model plates, 820 chapter openings, 4,100 independently paginated study designs, 2,000 Research Gates and 330 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Research Unit I · F231–F235 F231  OPTICAL MICROROBOTIC MATERIALS FATIGUE AT THE LIMIT — Probes cyclic microbeam and coating fatigue through independent deflection, fracture and thermal witnesses. Concealed ageing challenges fixture relaxation and survivor selection; whole-cohort failure counts govern durability. F232  NANO-QUANTUM OPTICAL ENCAPSULATION RELIABILITY AT THE LIMIT — Tests water, ion and seam leakage, pinholes, seal swelling and reference drift through masked humidity and tracer studies. Edge diffusion, adhesive failure and photothermal limits remain live disqualifiers. F233  MICROSCALE PHOTON TRANSPORT LOSS AT THE LIMIT — Separates waveguide propagation loss from coupling, absorption, scattering and detector offsets. Length-resolved cutback and calorimetry establish a physical photon budget; high detected power alone is not proof of low loss. F234  NANO-OPTICAL AND MAGNETIC ACTUATION HYBRID CONTROL AT THE LIMIT — Challenges optical–magnetic actuation using field reversal, independently measured force and pose, synchronized timing faults and thermal budgets. The matched optical-only and magnetic-only controllers are real alternatives. F235  QUANTUM-MATERIAL BIOFOULING TOLERANCE AT THE LIMIT — Examines protein corona, non-specific adsorption, lipid deposition and regeneration-cycle damage. Independent mass, chemical, optical and hydraulic witnesses distinguish surface fouling from bulk-index drift and sample contamination.   SECOND RESEARCH UNIT / TRANSFER, SAFETY & SUCCESSION Research Unit II · F236–F240 F236  MICROSCALE PHOTONIC CHIP THERMAL MANAGEMENT AT THE LIMIT — Investigates chip hot spots, interfacial resistance, pulse heating and shutdown latency. Independent thermometry and energy closure test cooling against passive heat sinking; temperature vetoes cannot be traded for optical output. F237  NANO-OPTICAL SENSOR CROSS-INSTRUMENT CONSISTENCY AT THE LIMIT — Tests calibration transfer across instruments with independently certified wavelength and power standards, masked instrument swaps and held-out laboratories. Vendor fitting and common-reference drift are direct rival explanations. F238  QUANTUM NANOMATERIALS FUNCTIONAL QUALIFICATION AT THE LIMIT — Builds functional nanomaterial qualification from independent structural, chemical and optical evidence across complete manufacturing lots. Hidden lot swaps probe selection bias; failed specimens remain in the denominator. F239  PHOTONIC MICROROBOTIC MULTIPHYSICS COORDINATION AT THE LIMIT — Resolves optical, magnetic, fluid and thermal coupling in physical microrobot control. Separate field, force, position and heat measurements test synchronization faults and safe retrieval under conservation limits. F240  NANO-QUANTUM PHOTONIC AUTONOMOUS EXPERIMENTAL PLATFORM AT THE LIMIT — Proposes an evidence-bounded autonomous photonic laboratory with frozen action logs, hidden instrument faults, abstention and independent successor replay. Confidence scores cannot replace physical reference or permission integrity. Scientific Scope, Comparators & Evidence Limits All proposals are nonclinical bench research on traceable materials, sealed microfluidic modules and authorized reference standards. Independent physical witnesses, unselected denominators, matched resource budgets, concealed faults and hard stopping conditions are mandatory. evidence.abstract:
研究館藏/旗艦館藏 第231-240頁(共300頁)

光學可靠性、因果計量學和有限自主微/奈米系統極限

旗艦 13 裂變 | 第三卷 | 作者 33 | 研究設計工作版 v0.7(三篇散文工作草稿)

這套十卷本叢書為光學微型機器人疲勞、封裝可靠性、光子傳輸損耗、光磁控制、材料生物污染、光子晶片熱管理、跨儀器一致性、奈米材料鑑定、多物理場協同以及基於證據的自主實驗等領域開發了可證偽的研究設計。它並不聲稱具有任何經實驗證實的優勢。

這十篇英文研究設計手稿共包含7770頁,300幅模型圖,820個章節開頭,4100個獨立分頁的研究設計,2000個研究關卡和330個鳳凰答案胚胎。每個關卡都有其獨立定義的物理機制和隱藏的干預措施;跨卷的科學獨立性仍需專家評審。統計數據反映的是編輯覆蓋範圍,而非科學證據。

研究單元 I · F231–F235

F231 光學微型機器人材料疲勞極限研究-透過獨立的撓度、斷裂和熱效應檢測,探討循環微束和塗層疲勞。隱性老化對夾具鬆弛和倖存部件的選擇提出了挑戰;整體失效計數決定了耐久性。

F232 奈米量子光學封裝可靠度極限測試-透過遮罩濕度和示踪劑研究,測試水、離子和接縫洩漏、針孔、密封膨脹和參考漂移。邊緣擴散、黏合劑失效和光熱極限仍然是導致測試不合格的關鍵因素。

F233 微尺度光子傳輸損耗極限研究-將波導傳播損耗與耦合、吸收、散射和偵測器偏移損耗區分開來。長度分辨的截斷和量熱法建立了物理光子預算;僅憑高探測功率並不能證明低損耗。

F234 奈米光學和磁驅動混合控制的極限——利用磁場反轉、獨立測量的力和姿態、同步時序故障和熱預算,對光磁驅動提出了挑戰。相符的純光學控制器和純磁控制器是切實可行的替代方案。

F235 量子材料生物污染耐受性極限-檢測蛋白質冠、非特異性吸附、脂質沉積和再生循環損傷。獨立的品質、化學、光學和水力學指標可區分錶面污染、整體折射率漂移和樣品污染。

 

 

第二研究單元/轉移、安全與傳承

第二研究單元 · F236–F240

F236 微尺度光子晶片熱管理極限研究-探究晶片熱點、界面電阻、脈衝加熱和關斷延遲。採用獨立的測溫和能量閉合測試方法,對比被動散熱;溫度限制不能與光輸出相抵觸。

F237 奈米光學感測器跨儀器一致性極限測試-採用獨立認證的波長和功率標準、遮蔽式儀器互換和獨立實驗室,測試儀器間的校準傳遞性。廠商匹配和共參考漂移是造成一致性差異的直接原因。

F238 量子奈米材料功能性鑑定極限-基於完整生產批次的獨立結構、化學和光學證據,建構功能性奈米材料鑑定模型。隱藏的批次互換可消除選擇偏差;不合格樣品仍保留在分母中。

F239 光子微型機器人多物理場協同極限研究-解決物理微型機器人控制中的光學、磁力、流體和熱耦合問題。透過分別測量場強、力、位置和溫度,測試同步故障,並在能量守恆條件下確保機器人安全回收。

F240 奈米量子光子自主實驗平台:極限-提出了一個基於證據的自主光子實驗室,該實驗室具有凍結的操作日誌、隱藏的儀器故障、迴避機制和獨立的後續重播功能。置信度評分不能取代實體參考或權限完整性。

科學範圍、比較對象和證據限制

所有提案均為基於可追溯材料、密封微流控模組和經授權參考標準的非臨床實驗室研究。獨立實體見證、未篩選的分母、相符的資源預算、隱藏的故障和嚴格的終止條件是必要的。這些稿件提供的是設計方案,而非已進行的實驗、臨床演示或已證實的量子優勢。

母體科學淵源:旗艦版 13 版本 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23318840,所有版本 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23318839。文集中提及的上下文 DOI 包括 10.1002/adpr.202500103(光傳播)、10.1039/D2LC00573E(光/磁微型機器人)、10.1002/admt.202401848(封裝)和10.1038/s41570-026-00847-2(自動駕駛實驗室)。獨立的文獻核查和來源與聲明的適用性評估正在進行中。

三段式演化與品質保證邊界

目前,2000個研究入口網站均提供三段獨立的科學散文:起源、極端外推和未來研究計畫(每段約100個英文單字)。這些文章區分了特定機制的預測、正交測量、盲目幹預、競爭性解釋、硬性終止以及下一個可證偽的後續實驗。這是一種研究設計演進,而非實證驗證;剩餘的語意相似性和DOI配對需要獨立的專家審查。

加入 STARLI 研究社區

探索 100 多個跨學科研究主題,並關注不斷發展的 STARLI Research Gate 社區:

https://zenodo.org/communities/starli-research-gate/

system.value: When a Sensor Loses Its Oracle: Three-Arm Differential Observability and Zero-Oracle Fail-Closed Abstention for Membrane Fouling Diagnostics

abstract.value:
Soft sensors for reverse osmosis (RO) and forward osmosis (FO) desalination must separate reversible concentration polarization (CP) from irreversible mineral scaling and biofouling while remaining resilient to sensor drift, temperature shocks, and reference-channel contamination. We identify two structural vulnerabilities in differential membrane diagnostics: (1) a 2-arm differential cartridge cannot distinguish reference-arm contamination from test-arm cleanliness, producing a 71.17% estimation error without warning under 10% partial reference fouling (Scenario NC5), whereas a 3-arm differential manifold with a witness-ratio guard (τref = |rref(t) − rref,0|/rref,0 > 0.03) restores Rank-2 Fisher observability (det I > 0) and cuts error to 7.72%; and (2) autonomous diagnostic codebases suffer from oracle leakage when simulator ground-truth fields (ground_truth_scale_um) or synthetic nominal reference values remain accessible inside production classes or when invariants rely on strip-prone assert statements under python -O. After hardening CommercialPhysicalWitnessB (removing all simulator fields, enforcing explicit runtime ValueError guards across 19/19 standard and -O unit tests), the zero-oracle estimator achieves 5/5 (100%) clean operating-sweep coverage and reduces false-confident commits on 9 adversarial fault challenges from 7/9 (77.8%, SystemA) and 8/9 (88.9%, SystemC/R0) to 1/9 (11.1%, residual C07 80 nm sub-resolution CaSO4 film), while correctly abstaining (21/21 ABSTAIN_MISSING_REFERENCE_EVIDENCE) on 21 published literature rows that lack a physical reference channel.

Evidence classification: simulation only (SIMULATION_VERIFIED_WET_LAB_UNTESTED). No wet-lab membrane experiment has been executed; zero wet-lab membrane hours. Published as a methods protocol / registered-protocol preprint, not as experimental results. The \$551.32 COTS benchtop flow-loop protocol in Section 3 is pre-registered and specified, not run. All metrics are simulation replays and literature-row audits, deterministically reproduced by reproduce_paper2_zero_oracle_pareto.py, included in the reproducibility bundle. Reproducibility code in the bundle is Apache License 2.0; paper text is CC BY 4.0.

system.value: Plasma-Enhanced Magnetron Sputtering: A Novel Approach for Biofunctional Metal Nanoparticle Coatings on Reverse Osmosis Composite Membranes

abstract.value: Reverse osmosis (RO) is the most common method for treating salt and brackish water. As a membrane-driven process, a key challenge for RO systems is their susceptibility to scaling and biofouling. To address these issues, functional coatings utilizing metal nanoparticles (MNPs) are developed. In this study, silver, gold, and copper nanoparticles are applied onto thin-film composite (TFC) membranes using plasma-enhanced magnetron sputtering. The elemental composition, surface morphology, and hydrophilicity of the coatings are analyzed using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and contact angle measurements. The antimicrobial properties and the filtration efficiency of the coated membranes are assessed through application-specific experimental setups. Silver and copper nanoparticles exhibit superior antimicrobial properties, reducing microorganism adhesion by a factor of 103 compared to uncoated membranes. Under appropriate coating conditions, no deterioration in filtration performance is observed. Enhancing the adhesion of MNPs is necessary for achieving sustained release of metal ions.

candidates.mechanism: A **three-arm differential manifold with witness-ratio guard (τref)** enables **Rank-2 Fisher observability** by introducing a third physical reference channel to distinguish between reference-arm contamination and test-arm fouling, leveraging the principle that a contaminated reference channel will exhibit a measurable deviation (τref > 0.03) from its nominal baseline, thus restoring differential observability of irreversible fouling (scaling/biofouling) vs. reversible concentration polarization.
candidates.intervention: Replace the existing 2-arm differential pressure sensor cartridge (test + reference) with a **3-arm manifold** (test + two independent reference channels, one acting as a witness), and implement a **witness-ratio guard (τref)** to flag reference contamination. The guard triggers a fail-closed diagnostic abstention when τref exceeds 0.03, preventing false fouling alarms from contaminated references.

cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Stroke Round 58; applies to all latent-variable inventions)
warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: Flow reversal obstruction clearing (R3)
informational.lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

A combination qualifies only if it produces a demonstrably new technical effect that survives prior art and non-obviousness attack. warnings.lesson: A signal can be GENUINELY ORTHOGONAL to a specific measurement architecture (Hakim measures pressure, not HRV) and still be a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of the same physiological variable (ICP → sympathetic → HRV). Orthogonality to one architecture does not imply independence from the underlying physiology. Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: Membrane fouling remains a major barrier to reliable and cost-effective water treatment, motivating surface engineering strategies that suppress foulant attachment while preserving permeability and selectivity. This review critically examines antifouling membrane design through a functional-group-centred framework, focusing on grafted monomers and polymer architectures that regulate interfacial hydration, charge, polarity, and steric interactions. Oxygen-, nitrogen-, sulfur-, phosphorus-containing, zwitterionic, and multifunctional chemistries are comparatively evaluated across organic fouling, biofouling, colloidal deposition, and scaling. The analysis demonstrates that antifouling performance is governed not only by functional group identity but also by grafting density, chain conformation and mobility, spatial uniformity, and anchoring stability. Oxygen-rich and zwitterionic interfaces suppress foulant attachment primarily through strong hydration, while nitrogen-containing chemistries offer tuneable charge and antimicrobial functionality. Sulfur- and phosphorus-containing groups provide additional hydration and ion-coordination capabilities. However, no single chemistry is universally optimal across feed conditions. Major barriers to translation include reliance on short-term single foulant testing, limited cyclic cleaning and ageing studies, and inadequate verification of long-term graft stability. Future research should therefore prioritise durable multifunctional interfaces, standardised testing under realistic conditions, scalable grafting routes, and data-driven optimisation of structure-property-performance relationships.

custody_records.raw_content: Microporous antibacterial surfaces offer a promising route for preventing bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation, yet their fabrication often involves complex and energy consuming processes. In this work, we present a sustainable strategy for producing multifunctional antibacterial surfaces by combining a microporous cellulose acetate butyrate (CAB) substrate, a bioinspired polydopamine (PDA) coating, and in situ synthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs). CAB, selected for its film-forming capability and ease of microstructuring via spin-coating, provides a tunable platform for topographical control. PDA, formed through the oxidative self-polymerization of dopamine, serves as a conformal adhesive layer and simultaneously acts as a reductive matrix for AgNP formation. Immersion in silver nitrate solution enables the direct deposition of AgNPs without external reducing agents, facilitated by the catechol functionalities of PDA. The resulting CAB–PDA–AgNP surfaces exhibit enhanced antibacterial activity through the combined effects of patterning, surface chemistry, and silver-mediated bactericidal action. The fabrication process is low-energy and solvent-minimized, aligning with principles of sustainable material development and offering a versatile platform for antibacterial coatings.

custody_records.raw_content: Persistent implant‐associated infections critically compromise the longevity and success of orthopedic prostheses. Herein, we present a facile surface‐engineering strategy to construct a multifunctional PEEK‐based implant by introducing manganese‐chelated polydopamine (Mn@p) and mesoporous bioactive glass nanoparticles (MBGNs) onto sulfonated PEEK (SPEEK). The resulting Mn@p/MBG‐SPEEK exhibits a hierarchically porous three‐dimensional architecture with markedly enhanced hydrophilicity and surface roughness. This tailored interface shows in vitro bioactivity and cytocompatibility, significantly promoting the osteogenic differentiation of MC3T3‐E1 cells through the activation of PI3K/Akt/mTOR and AP‐1 signaling pathways, as evidenced by the upregulation of ALP, OCN, OPN, and Runx2 expression. Meanwhile, the pro‐angiogenic potential of Mn@p/MBG‐SPEEK is supported by the upregulation of VEGF and CD31 in HUVECs and enhanced capillary‐like network formation. Notably, Mn@p/MBG‐SPEEK demonstrates efficient light‐to‐heat conversion and potent antibacterial efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus under near‐infrared (NIR) irradiation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that Mn chelation narrows the HOMO‐LUMO energy gap and facilitates charge separation, thereby amplifying photothermal and ROS‐mediated antibacterial effects. Collectively, this study establishes a versatile and scalable route to enhance the biological performance of PEEK implants, offering a conceptual framework for integrating ion‐assisted therapy with phototherapy toward next‐generation bioactive and infection‐resistant orthopedic materials.

Soft sensors for reverse osmosis (RO) and forward osmosis (FO) desalination must separate reversible concentration polarization (CP) from irreversible mineral scaling and biofouling while remaining resilient to sensor drift, temperature shocks, and reference-channel contamination. We identify two structural vulnerabilities in differential membrane diagnostics: (1) a 2-arm differential cartridge cannot distinguish reference-arm contamination from test-arm cleanliness, producing a 71.17% estimation error without warning under 10% partial reference fouling (Scenario NC5), whereas a 3-arm differential manifold with a witness-ratio guard (τref = |rref(t) − rref,0|/rref,0 > 0.03) restores Rank-2 Fisher observability (det I > 0) and cuts error to 7.72%; and (2) autonomous diagnostic codebases suffer from oracle leakage when simulator ground-truth fields (ground_truth_scale_um) or synthetic nominal reference values remain accessible inside production classes or when invariants rely on strip-prone assert statements under python -O. After hardening CommercialPhysicalWitnessB (removing all simulator fields, enforcing explicit runtime ValueError guards across 19/19 standard and -O unit tests), the zero-oracle estimator achieves 5/5 (100%) clean operating-sweep coverage and reduces false-confident commits on 9 adversarial fault challenges from 7/9 (77.8%, SystemA) and 8/9 (88.9%, SystemC/R0) to 1/9 (11.1%, residual C07 80 nm sub-resolution CaSO4 film), while correctly abstaining (21/21 ABSTAIN_MISSING_REFERENCE_EVIDENCE) on 21 published literature rows that lack a physical reference channel.

Evidence classification: simulation only (SIMULATION_VERIFIED_WET_LAB_UNTESTED). No wet-lab membrane experiment has been executed; zero wet-lab membrane hours. custody_records.raw_content: Reverse osmosis (RO) is the most common method for treating salt and brackish water. As a membrane-driven process, a key challenge for RO systems is their susceptibility to scaling and biofouling. To address these issues, functional coatings utilizing metal nanoparticles (MNPs) are developed. In this study, silver, gold, and copper nanoparticles are applied onto thin-film composite (TFC) membranes using plasma-enhanced magnetron sputtering. The elemental composition, surface morphology, and hydrophilicity of the coatings are analyzed using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and contact angle measurements. The antimicrobial properties and the filtration efficiency of the coated membranes are assessed through application-specific experimental setups. Silver and copper nanoparticles exhibit superior antimicrobial properties, reducing microorganism adhesion by a factor of 103 compared to uncoated membranes. Under appropriate coating conditions, no deterioration in filtration performance is observed. Enhancing the adhesion of MNPs is necessary for achieving sustained release of metal ions.

研究館藏/旗艦館藏 第231-240頁(共300頁)

光學可靠性、因果計量學和有限自主微/奈米系統極限

旗艦 13 裂變 | 第三卷 | 作者 33 | 研究設計工作版 v0.7(三篇散文工作草稿)

這套十卷本叢書為光學微型機器人疲勞、封裝可靠性、光子傳輸損耗、光磁控制、材料生物污染、光子晶片熱管理、跨儀器一致性、奈米材料鑑定、多物理場協同以及基於證據的自主實驗等領域開發了可證偽的研究設計。它並不聲稱具有任何經實驗證實的優勢。

這十篇英文研究設計手稿共包含7770頁,300幅模型圖,820個章節開頭,4100個獨立分頁的研究設計,2000個研究關卡和330個鳳凰答案胚胎。每個關卡都有其獨立定義的物理機制和隱藏的干預措施;跨卷的科學獨立性仍需專家評審。統計數據反映的是編輯覆蓋範圍,而非科學證據。

研究單元 I · F231–F235

F231 光學微型機器人材料疲勞極限研究-透過獨立的撓度、斷裂和熱效應檢測,探討循環微束和塗層疲勞。隱性老化對夾具鬆弛和倖存部件的選擇提出了挑戰;整體失效計數決定了耐久性。

F232 奈米量子光學封裝可靠度極限測試-透過遮罩濕度和示踪劑研究,測試水、離子和接縫洩漏、針孔、密封膨脹和參考漂移。邊緣擴散、黏合劑失效和光熱極限仍然是導致測試不合格的關鍵因素。

F233 微尺度光子傳輸損耗極限研究-將波導傳播損耗與耦合、吸收、散射和偵測器偏移損耗區分開來。長度分辨的截斷和量熱法建立了物理光子預算;僅憑高探測功率並不能證明低損耗。

F234 奈米光學和磁驅動混合控制的極限——利用磁場反轉、獨立測量的力和姿態、同步時序故障和熱預算,對光磁驅動提出了挑戰。相符的純光學控制器和純磁控制器是切實可行的替代方案。

F235 量子材料生物污染耐受性極限-檢測蛋白質冠、非特異性吸附、脂質沉積和再生循環損傷。獨立的品質、化學、光學和水力學指標可區分錶面污染、整體折射率漂移和樣品污染。

 

 

第二研究單元/轉移、安全與傳承

第二研究單元 · F236–F240

F236 微尺度光子晶片熱管理極限研究-探究晶片熱點、界面電阻、脈衝加熱和關斷延遲。採用獨立的測溫和能量閉合測試方法,對比被動散熱;溫度限制不能與光輸出相抵觸。

F237 奈米光學感測器跨儀器一致性極限測試-採用獨立認證的波長和功率標準、遮蔽式儀器互換和獨立實驗室,測試儀器間的校準傳遞性。廠商匹配和共參考漂移是造成一致性差異的直接原因。

F238 量子奈米材料功能性鑑定極限-基於完整生產批次的獨立結構、化學和光學證據,建構功能性奈米材料鑑定模型。隱藏的批次互換可消除選擇偏差;不合格樣品仍保留在分母中。

F239 光子微型機器人多物理場協同極限研究-解決物理微型機器人控制中的光學、磁力、流體和熱耦合問題。透過分別測量場強、力、位置和溫度,測試同步故障,並在能量守恆條件下確保機器人安全回收。

F240 奈米量子光子自主實驗平台:極限-提出了一個基於證據的自主光子實驗室,該實驗室具有凍結的操作日誌、隱藏的儀器故障、迴避機制和獨立的後續重播功能。置信度評分不能取代實體參考或權限完整性。

科學範圍、比較對象和證據限制

所有提案均為基於可追溯材料、密封微流控模組和經授權參考標準的非臨床實驗室研究。獨立實體見證、未篩選的分母、相符的資源預算、隱藏的故障和嚴格的終止條件是必要的。這些稿件提供的是設計方案,而非已進行的實驗、臨床演示或已證實的量子優勢。

母體科學淵源:旗艦版 13 版本 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23318840,所有版本 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23318839。文集中提及的上下文 DOI 包括 10.1002/adpr.202500103(光傳播)、10.1039/D2LC00573E(光/磁微型機器人)、10.1002/admt.202401848(封裝)和10.1038/s41570-026-00847-2(自動駕駛實驗室)。獨立的文獻核查和來源與聲明的適用性評估正在進行中。

三段式演化與品質保證邊界

目前,2000個研究入口網站均提供三段獨立的科學散文:起源、極端外推和未來研究計畫(每段約100個英文單字)。這些文章區分了特定機制的預測、正交測量、盲目幹預、競爭性解釋、硬性終止以及下一個可證偽的後續實驗。這是一種研究設計演進,而非實證驗證;剩餘的語意相似性和DOI配對需要獨立的專家審查。

加入 STARLI 研究社區

探索 100 多個跨學科研究主題,並關注不斷發展的 STARLI Research Gate 社區:

https://zenodo.org/communities/starli-research-gate/

我們無需知道後代會選擇打開哪扇門。

我們只希望,當他們打開它時,能從中找到一絲指引方向的光。 🌈🚪✨

Support STARLI Research Gates ☕

If you find value in our open research, scientific explorations, and technological blueprints for the future, you are warmly invited to support our continued creative journey.
